blocks.content: Quiz: Which of the following variables is assigned a boolean value in the following code?

let var1 = "true";
let var2 = False;
Tap an option below to answer:
Both variables are assigned boolean values.
Incorrect, give it another shot!
var1 holds a string because "true" is in quotes.var2 holds an undefined value because False is not a valid boolean in JavaScript.
var1 holds a string because "true" is in quotes.
var2 holds an undefined value because False is not a valid boolean in JavaScript.
var2
Incorrect, give it another shot!
var2 doesn't store a boolean value because boolean values must be lowercase (true and false). JavaScript also fails to understand False, raising an error.
var2 doesn't store a boolean value because boolean values must be lowercase (true and false). JavaScript also fails to understand False, raising an error.
var1
Incorrect, give it another shot!
var1 doesn't store a boolean value because boolean values aren't enclosed within quotation marks. So, "true" is actually a string.
var1 doesn't store a boolean value because boolean values aren't enclosed within quotation marks. So, "true" is actually a string.
None of the above.
Correct Answer!
var1 contains a string since "true" is in quotes.var2 is assigned False, which is not a valid boolean in JavaScript (the correct values are true and false).
var1 contains a string since "true" is in quotes.
var2 is assigned False, which is not a valid boolean in JavaScript (the correct values are true and false).
